pack.description: Vocabulary of ecology passages and talks: populations, food webs and relationships between species.
pack.selection_note: Internal selection of terms that recur in introductory ecology texts; this is not an official list and CEFR levels are author estimates.
pack.copyright_policy: Original content written for this app. No dictionary definition, ETS item or external word list was copied.

entries.definition: all the living things in an area together with the place where they live, seen as one system
entries.example_academic: Removing a single species can destabilize an entire ecosystem.
entries.example_spoken: The lake's ecosystem still hasn't recovered from the spill.

entries.definition: the natural place where a particular plant or animal lives
entries.example_academic: The species has lost more than half of its natural habitat in thirty years.
entries.example_spoken: These frogs only breed in a very specific habitat.

entries.definition: an animal that hunts, kills and eats other animals
entries.example_academic: In the absence of predators, the deer population doubled within a decade.
entries.example_spoken: Owls are the main predators of mice around here.

entries.definition: an animal that is hunted and eaten by another animal
entries.example_academic: The spider detects its prey through vibrations in the web.
entries.example_spoken: Rabbits are easy prey for foxes.

entries.definition: the variety of plant and animal life in a particular place
entries.example_academic: Tropical forests contain a disproportionate share of the planet's biodiversity.
entries.example_spoken: The new park is supposed to protect local biodiversity.

entries.definition: the particular role and place that a living thing has within its surroundings
entries.example_academic: Two species rarely occupy exactly the same niche for long.
entries.example_spoken: Each bird has its own niche, so they don't really compete.

entries.definition: the regular seasonal movement of animals from one region to another
entries.example_academic: The timing of the migration depends on day length rather than temperature.
entries.example_spoken: We saw thousands of geese during the fall migration.

entries.definition: to move around searching for food
entries.example_academic: Bees forage over a wider area when flowers are scarce.
entries.example_spoken: Squirrels forage for nuts all over the quad.

entries.definition: the highest layer of branches and leaves in a forest
entries.example_academic: Many rainforest species spend their entire lives in the canopy.
entries.example_spoken: Hardly any light gets through the canopy.

entries.definition: to be slowly destroyed by natural processes after death
entries.example_academic: Fallen leaves decompose and return nutrients to the soil.
entries.example_spoken: Plastic takes centuries to decompose.

entries.definition: describing a plant or animal that arrives in a new area and spreads in a harmful way
entries.example_academic: Invasive plants often outcompete native vegetation for light and water.
entries.example_spoken: That vine is invasive; it's taking over the whole garden.

entries.definition: an animal that feeds on dead animals it did not kill itself
entries.example_academic: Scavengers play a crucial role by removing carcasses that could spread disease.
entries.example_spoken: Vultures are scavengers, not hunters.

entries.definition: to live in the same place at the same time
entries.example_academic: The two species coexist because they feed at different times of day.
entries.example_spoken: Wolves and farmers have to learn to coexist.

entries.definition: an area that an animal or group defends as its own
entries.example_academic: Males mark the boundaries of their territory with scent.
entries.example_spoken: The cat next door thinks our yard is part of its territory.

entries.definition: an area of land that is covered with shallow water for much of the year
entries.example_academic: Wetlands filter pollutants and absorb floodwater.
entries.example_spoken: They want to drain the wetland to build a parking lot.

entries.definition: the situation in which a kind of plant or animal no longer exists
entries.example_academic: Habitat destruction is now the leading cause of extinction.
entries.example_spoken: The species was saved from extinction by a breeding program.

entries.definition: a close relationship between two different living things in which each gains something
entries.example_academic: The symbiosis between the fungus and the tree roots benefits both partners.
entries.example_spoken: It's a kind of symbiosis: the bird gets food and the buffalo gets cleaned.

entries.definition: relating to feeding and the positions that living things occupy in a food chain
entries.example_academic: Energy is lost at each trophic level, which limits the length of food chains.
entries.example_spoken: Plants are at the lowest trophic level, right?

entries.definition: a very large natural region with its own typical climate, plants and animals
entries.example_academic: The tundra biome is characterized by low temperatures and a short growing season.
entries.example_spoken: Which biome gets the least rain, desert or tundra?

entries.definition: living on or in another living thing and taking food from it while harming it
entries.example_academic: Parasitic wasps lay their eggs inside the bodies of caterpillars.
entries.example_spoken: It's a parasitic plant, so it has no leaves of its own.

entries.definition: a relationship between two species in which both benefit
entries.example_academic: Pollination is a classic example of mutualism between plants and insects.
entries.example_spoken: So in mutualism nobody loses, unlike with parasites.

entries.definition: found naturally in one particular place and nowhere else
entries.example_academic: The island supports dozens of endemic species that evolved in isolation.
entries.example_spoken: This lizard is endemic to one small valley.

entries.definition: relating to or living on the banks of a river
entries.example_academic: Riparian vegetation stabilizes the banks and shades the water.
entries.example_spoken: They're replanting the riparian zone along the creek.

entries.definition: an insect or other animal that carries the fine powder from one flower to another so that seeds can form
entries.example_academic: A decline in pollinators threatens the yield of many fruit crops.
entries.example_spoken: Bees are the best-known pollinators, but bats do it too.

entries.definition: a kind of plant or animal whose presence has a very large effect on the whole community around it
entries.example_academic: The sea otter is a keystone species because it controls the animals that destroy kelp forests.
entries.example_spoken: If you remove a keystone species, everything else falls apart.

entries.definition: the largest number of individuals that an area can support over a long time
entries.example_academic: Once the herd exceeded the carrying capacity of the island, starvation followed.
entries.example_spoken: The park has reached its carrying capacity for deer.

entries.definition: an animal at the very top of a food chain, which no other animal hunts
entries.example_academic: The return of an apex predator changed the behavior of grazing animals.
entries.example_spoken: Sharks are the apex predators in that reef.

entries.definition: the ability to produce many young
entries.example_academic: High fecundity compensates for the low survival rate of the young.
entries.example_spoken: Rabbits are famous for their fecundity.

entries.definition: dead plant and animal material that collects on the ground or in water
entries.example_academic: Worms and fungi convert detritus into nutrients that plants can absorb.
entries.example_spoken: The stream bed is covered in leaves and other detritus.
